US envoys Witkoff, Kushner arrive in Kyiv after talks to Putin in Moscow
Saturday’s meeting in Moscow lasted more than three hours behind closed doors and ended without announcements of any breakthroughs
US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held “encouraging” talks in Kyiv on Sunday in their first official visit to Ukraine as part of a renewed push to end more than 4½ years of Russia’s full-scale invasion.
Their trip follows a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Saturday, seeking to revive peace talks during escalating aerial attacks by both sides. Washington’s push to end the fighting has lost momentum, with the Trump administration focused for the past six months on the Iran war.
Russia has recently been using fast-flying, jet-powered drones, and the recurring wail of air-raid sirens has become part of daily life in Kyiv. Troops have struggled to make progress along the 1,250km (775-mile) front line.
Following two rounds of discussion with the U.S. officials, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the goal was a “just, fair peace” that would ensure there was “never an opportunity to resume aggression against Ukraine”.
He also thanked the American negotiators, who travelled by train, for coming to Kyiv, their first time in Ukraine. Zelensky said the next round of talks later on Sunday would bring in national security advisers from Britain, France and Germany.
“We’ve had very meaningful discussion, substantive, important, and we’re very encouraged,” Witkoff said.

articles.title: Azerbaijan starts local production of naval drones
articles.body:
- Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev toured a joint Azerbaijani-Turkish production facility building SALVO and KAYRA unmanned surface vessels on September 6.
- The facility, run by Azerbaijan's MIRAS and Turkey's DEARSAN Shipyard, marks a shift from importing Turkish naval drones to producing them domestically.
Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev visited the country’s navy on September 6, where officials showed him two unmanned surface vessels now being built inside Azerbaijan through a joint production line with a Turkish shipbuilder.
Aliyev and First Lady Mehriban Aliyeva were briefed on the SALVO armed unmanned surface vessel and the KAYRA kamikaze unmanned surface vessel at a facility jointly operated by MIRAS Military-Industrial Company, a state defense manufacturer under Azerbaijan’s Ministry of Defense, and Turkey’s DEARSAN Shipyard.
Defense Minister Col. Gen. Zakir Hasanov briefed the president on the visit, according to a statement from the presidential press service. The two leaders toured the production line and watched the vessels undergo practical testing, and the statement did not disclose how many units of either vessel have been built or when full-rate production is expected to begin.
The SALVO is a Turkish-designed unmanned boat that first completed live-fire testing in 2022, when it struck a moving target in the Sea of Marmara using a Roketsan Cirit 70mm laser-guided missile fired from a remote turret, alongside a stabilized 12.7mm machine gun made by Aselsan. Built with a composite hull roughly 15 meters (49 feet) long, the vessel can reach speeds up to 60 knots and operate out to about 300 nautical miles (555 kilometers) from its controllers, who can run it from shore-based command posts or from other ships.
Dearsan has marketed the SALVO for reconnaissance, surface warfare, facility patrol and armed escort missions. Azerbaijan’s navy first publicly displayed a Turkish-built SALVO during a live-fire exercise in the Caspian Sea in August 2025, though it was not clear at the time when Baku had acquired the vessel.
The KAYRA is smaller and built for a different purpose. At about 7 meters (23 feet) long with a composite hull, it can reach a top speed of 50 knots and operate out to roughly 200 nautical miles (370 kilometers), according to Dearsan’s own specifications. Rather than carrying a separate weapons system, the KAYRA is designed as a one-way attack vessel, packed with its own warhead and intended to ram and destroy enemy ships, patrol boats, port infrastructure or naval bases directly.
Wednesday’s visit marks a shift from Azerbaijan simply operating Turkish-built naval drones to producing them jointly on Azerbaijani soil. The Ministry of Defense-linked MIRAS has increasingly partnered with Turkish defense firms in recent years, part of a broader defense-industrial relationship between Baku and Ankara that expanded significantly following Turkey’s military support to Azerbaijan during the 2020 war over Nagorno-Karabakh. Azerbaijan has separately developed its own smaller kamikaze drone boats, including the Kalan and Sugovushan models shown at a defense exhibition in 2024, though those remain considerably smaller than the Turkish-designed SALVO and KAYRA.

articles.title: Israeli strikes kill four, destroy hospital in southern Lebanon
articles.body:
Breadcrumb
Israeli strikes kill four, destroy hospital in southern Lebanon
Israeli strikes across southern Lebanon killed four people and wounded 20 on Sunday, Lebanon’s health ministry said, after the Israeli army issued its first evacuation order in several weeks and claimed it was responding to alleged Hezbollah drone attacks.
Two women were killed in the town of Arab Salim, in Nabatieh district, while two other people were killed in Nabatieh al-Fawqa, the ministry said. The provisional toll included several women and three children among the injured, with casualties also reported in Nabatieh and Kfar Rumman.
At around 6am local time, the Israeli military ordered residents within 300 metres of a building in Arab Salim to leave, describing the site as a Hezbollah "facility" but providing no evidence for the claim.
The warning marked the first such evacuation order issued by Israel in Lebanon in several weeks. Lebanon’s state-run National News Agency (NNA) said Israeli warplanes struck a different house after the warning, destroying it and killing the two women, before subsequently attacking the building named in the Israeli notice.
The health ministry said six people, including two girls, were wounded in Arab Salim. In Nabatieh al-Fawqa, two people were killed and two injured, while further casualties were reported in Nabatieh’s al-Rahibat neighbourhood and in Kfar Rumman.
Israel said it had launched the strikes after Hezbollah fired two drones towards Israeli troops operating in southern Lebanon. It accused the group of a "blatant violation" of the ceasefire framework, although no Israeli casualties were reported.
Civilian infrastructure hit
In Nabatieh al-Fawqa, an Israeli strike destroyed part of the Ghandour hospital, according to NNA. The hospital had been out of service for years, but its destruction added to the devastation of civilian infrastructure in a district repeatedly subjected to Israeli attacks.
NNA also reported that a heavy strike in Nabatieh targeted a historic building and damaged offices used by the Lebanese finance and agriculture authorities, as well as nearby shops and cafes.
Israeli artillery later hit the outskirts of Aitaroun, the forested Jounine area and the Doha area of Kfar Rumman, all in or near Nabatieh district, where Israel has intensified attacks in recent days.
Sunday’s attacks came a day after Israeli strikes killed five people in southern Lebanon including an 18-year-old woman in Mayfadoun.
'Security zone' plans
The escalation coincided with reports that Israel’s military is considering a partial withdrawal from southern Lebanon, reducing the depth of its self-declared security zone from roughly 10km to between three and four kilometres from the border.
Israeli state broadcaster Kan reported that security officials had held internal discussions over creating a narrower zone, reportedly called the "Gray Line", following Israeli operations at the strategic Ali al-Taher ridge. Any redeployment would require political approval, the report said.
Israel claimed this week to have taken "operational control" of the ridge, which overlooks a large area of southeastern Lebanon and lies about 15km from the Israeli border. The military said it had cleared underground Hezbollah routes there, while Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said troops would remain in the security zone until Hezbollah was disarmed.
Lebanese authorities and rights groups have repeatedly condemned Israel’s continued air strikes and ground presence as violations of the ceasefire arrangement.
Israeli strikes have killed more than 4,300 people since Hezbollah entered the regional conflict in response to US-Israeli strikes on Iran in late February 2026.

articles.title: Witkoff and Kushner likely brought substantive proposal to Moscow – experts to RT (VIDEO)
articles.body:
Witkoff and Kushner likely brought substantive proposal to Moscow – experts to RT (VIDEO)
There are grounds for cautious optimism following Saturday’s talks between US President Donald Trump’s envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow, former Austrian Foreign Minister Karin Kneissl and ex-White House aide Steve Gill have told RT.
Trump’s son-in-law and the US special envoy likely presented concrete and well-developed ideas on ending the Ukraine conflict to the Russian leadership, Kneissl and Gill surmised.
According to Kremlin aide Yury Ushakov, the talks, which lasted over three hours and included formal discussions as well as an informal exchange over lunch, were “substantive, constructive, extremely candid and trusting.” Aside from the Ukraine conflict, the two sides are understood to have discussed economic cooperation and potential “major, mutually beneficial Russian-American projects.”
Witkoff and Kushner subsequently departed for Kiev, where they were slated to hold meetings with Vladimir Zelensky and other Ukrainian officials.
Speaking to RT on Sunday, former Austrian Foreign Minister Karin Kneissl said that “there is apparently something materializing because these two persons would not come without anything in their hands.” She also claimed that “trust is there” between Moscow and Washington, citing “this ongoing direct communication on a high-ranking political level.”
Kneissl also pointed to the previously unannounced visit to the Russian capital by CIA Director John Ratcliffe last Tuesday, during which he met with Russian Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR) chief Sergei Naryshkin.
On Sunday, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov likewise said that Saturday’s negotiations were indicative of an “atmosphere of trust” between Russia and the US.
Conservative media host Steve Gill, who served in the office of the US Trade Representative under Presidents George H. W. Bush and Bill Clinton, concurred with Kneissl, saying that he was “optimistic that the meeting took as long as it did.”
He told RT that the trip Witkoff and Kushner made to Moscow was likely preceded by considerable preparatory work, with Trump’s envoys plausibly bringing a substantive proposal to the Russian capital.
“The fact that it took three hours to kind of work through those details and now they’re heading to Ukraine leaves me at least optimistic that hopefully some progress was made today,” Gill concluded.

Russia’s hybrid attacks using bomb-laden drones against airports, agents in our cities, cyberattacks on our networks and sabotage of our infrastructure are a daily reality. These attacks will intensify, but we can protect ourselves

This includes not only interception, but also the neutralization of bombs carried by drones and explosive devices
In addition, according to available information, in the future, drone protection is to be the responsibility not only of the Federal Police and other authorities, but also of companies operating in critical infrastructure sectors.
Germany also plans to make greater use of artificial intelligence, biometric facial recognition and video systems to search for spies and people who may be preparing attacks. In addition, AI is to help automatically detect weapons and suspicious behavior.
Separately, plans also call for the creation of a national protective shield called "CyberDome"—a dense network of digital sensors for detecting and intercepting hacker attacks on government institutions and businesses.
We remind you

articles.title: Russia keeps building Su-34 fighter-bombers despite Ukraine war
articles.body:
- A newly built Su-34 fighter-bomber in factory primer was photographed at an air show in Novosibirsk, where the jet is manufactured.
- Russia had received 212 Su-34s by early 2026, including 18 delivered in 2025, continuing steady production despite the ongoing war in Ukraine.
Photos taken at an air show in Novosibirsk captured a newly built Su-34 fighter-bomber still in factory gray primer, adding to a steady stream of the twin-seat jets Russia has produced for its air force even as it continues fighting in Ukraine.
The aircraft was spotted at Mochishche Aerodrome in Novosibirsk during the 15th annual Viva Avia air festival, held August 1 and 2 to mark the 110th anniversary of Russian naval aviation and the 95th anniversary of Russia’s military transport aviation branch. The jet was built at the Novosibirsk Aviation Plant, known as NAZ or NAPO, the sole manufacturer of the Su-34 and part of Russia’s United Aircraft Corporation.
By the start of 2026, Russia’s air force had received a total of 212 Su-34s built at the Novosibirsk plant, including seven prototype and pre-production aircraft, according to available production figures. The plant delivered 16 production aircraft in 2024 and 18 more in 2025, a pace that has held roughly steady over the past several years despite Western sanctions targeting Russia’s defense industry.
Oryx, an open-source group that tracks visually confirmed military equipment losses in the war, has documented 43 Su-34s destroyed since Russia’s full-scale invasion began in February 2022, a figure that covers only losses supported by photographic or video evidence and likely understates the true total. At roughly 18 to 20 new aircraft a year, Russia’s current production pace has been running behind the confirmed combat loss rate for extended stretches of the war, according to open-source trackers.
The Su-34, known to NATO by the reporting name Fullback, is a twin-engine, two-seat fighter-bomber that replaced the older Su-24 in Russian service. It was formally accepted into the Russian military’s inventory in March 2014, following a program that traces back to a Soviet-era design contract signed in 1989. The aircraft carries a Sh141 phased-array radar, an L-150 Pastel radar warning receiver, and 12 hardpoints for weapons, and it can refuel in flight and operate from airfields without ground support equipment thanks to an onboard auxiliary power unit.
Production has continued through a series of contracts rather than one long-running deal. Russia’s defense ministry ordered 32 Su-34s in 2008, all delivered by 2013, followed by a second contract for 92 more aircraft due by 2020. A further order for 20 aircraft with upgraded electronic warfare equipment followed in 2020, and Russian media reported in prior years that at least 76 more Su-34s, upgraded under the Su-34M designation with new electronics and precision weapons carried in underwing pods, were expected to be delivered by 2027.
Russia has used the Su-34 extensively during its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, employing it to drop glide bombs on Ukrainian positions and cities from standoff ranges that keep the aircraft largely outside the reach of Ukrainian air defenses. The aircraft’s continued production, even in wartime, has made it one of the more closely tracked programs in open-source assessments of Russia’s defense industrial output.

Drone activity was also reported over temporarily occupied Crimea and the Black and Azov seas.
The operation coincided with a temporary Ukrainian commitment concerning Russian airspace during planned visits by US President Donald Trump’s representatives to Moscow and Kyiv.

articles.title: Witkoff, Kushner Cite ‘Significant Progress,’ Push Trilateral Peace Talks
articles.body:
US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner announced in Kyiv on Sunday, Sept. 6, that their negotiations in Moscow yielded “significant progress” and expressed optimism that a return to a trilateral negotiation format between the US, Ukraine, and Russia could be announced in the near future.
Speaking to journalists following high-level meetings in the Ukrainian capital with President Volodymyr Zelensky and European national security advisers, the American emissaries outlined the substance of their regional diplomatic mission.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
“I think we made significant progress in Moscow. We heard new ideas,” Witkoff said, according to Ukrinform, 24 Channel and European Pravda. 
“You heard President Zelensky talk about trilateral negotiations, which we hope will be announced shortly. There were many other important, compelling ideas that we discussed in Moscow and that were presented here in Kyiv. We believe cooperation is critical.”
Kushner, son-in-law to US President Donald Trump, described their meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Saturday evening as “very constructive and substantive.” He noted that discussions examined why earlier peace formulas had stalled while exploring the foundational conditions required for an enduring settlement.
“We really tried to think through what elements are needed for the durable peace we’ve been talking about,” Kushner said. “What Russia can get out of this, what Ukraine can get out of this, and what the world can get out of this. And it was a very good dialogue. We asked a lot of questions; he asked a lot of questions.”
Zelensky Opens Third Round of Kyiv Talks With UK, France, Germany
Kushner highlighted that returning to a formal trilateral diplomatic track represents a key objective for Washington. “One thing Steve and I believe is productive is returning to a trilateral format. We’ve spoken to both sides, so hopefully very soon we will achieve progress on this matter,” he stated.
Trump’s peace framework
Addressing the mechanics of their diplomacy, Kushner revealed that the American team maintains continuous, direct contact with Kyiv’s top security and diplomatic officials, even during periods when the envoys are not physically present in Ukraine.
“The fact that we hadn’t traveled [to Ukraine before now] does not mean we weren’t communicating,” Kushner explained. “The conversations we have with Rustem [Umerov], Kyrylo [Budanov], Davyd [Arakhamia], and Sergiy [Kyslytsya] happen on an almost daily basis.”
Kushner added that the delegation engages directly with President Zelensky whenever necessary, describing him as “very committed to making progress and making decisions.”
Relaying Trump’s perspective, Kushner emphasized that the US administration is seeking a durable, sustainable resolution rather than an unstable freeze.
“He wanted us to convey this: he understands that this is a very complex problem. But it is a problem that must be solved – not only to stop the fighting, but to create the conditions for a lasting and sustainable peace,” Kushner said.
Asked at a press conference whether the war could be brought to a close before winter, Kushner offered a measured outlook, noting that while success is not guaranteed, intensive efforts are underway.
“This is a very, very difficult problem, but we will try. And I think if we can achieve this, it will be incredible. That doesn’t mean we will achieve it, but it is a very important effort,” he said.
Multi-stage Kyiv consultations
Witkoff emphasized the importance of maintaining open dialogue across the geopolitical divide to narrow the gap between the warring parties.
“Putin and his team have always treated us with respect – relationships are critical to resolving conflicts,” Witkoff told.
“Both sides have to agree on this. Jared and my job is to bring the sides together, reduce the differences between them, and establish effective channels of communication. Hopefully, we have started this constructively over the last 48 hours. We are confident that a successful solution can be found.”
The envoys’ press availability followed a full day of multi-stage negotiations in Kyiv. The American delegation arrived overland by rail aboard the “Peace Express” after Russian air raids made landing by plane impossible to organize.
Consultations in Kyiv began with bilateral discussions between Zelensky and the American emissaries, followed by a multilateral session that included national security advisers from the UK, France, and Germany. The direct talks took place under an agreed temporary pause on aerial strikes targeting both capitals during the visit.

Israeli strikes on Lebanon kill several despite truce
September 6, 2026
At least four people were killed in Israeli strikes on Lebanon on Sunday, which comes despite a ceasefire between the two countries, according to the Lebanese Health Ministry.
The Lebanese officials also said around 20 other people, including children, were wounded in the strikes.
The office of Lebanon's President Joseph Aoun called the strikes a "dangerous escalation" that targeted "purely civilian administrations and health centers."
"President Aoun held the Israeli side fully responsible for this ongoing escalation, calling on the United States and the international community to take immediate action to stop these violations and hold the perpetrators accountable," his aides said in a statement.
In turn, the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said the strikes were a response to "a blatant violation" by Hezbollah militants.
"Terrorists from the Hezbollah terrorist organization launched two drones towards IDF soldiers operating in the Security Zone in southern Lebanon," the military said in a statement, adding that there were no reports of Israeli soldiers wounded.
What do we know about the strikes?
Early on Sunday morning, the Israeli military issued an online evacuation alert for Arab Salim, saying it identified a "Hezbollah facility" there.
Lebanon's state-run National News Agency (NNA) said the Israeli military subsequently carried out a strike on the building mentioned in the original evacuation warning.
NNA also reported that "enemy warplanes launched a strike on another house, destroying it." Two women were killed in the strike.
Another two people were killed in Israeli strikes near the town of Nabatieh al-Fawqa, which lies on the edge of Israel's "security zone" that it occupies in southern Lebanon.
Lebanon's Health Ministry said an Israeli strike "totally destroyed" a disused hospital. The Health Ministry called the incident "another grave violation of international humanitarian law."
The Israeli military said its targets included what it described as a Hezbollah command center inside a building that was previously used as a hospital, as well as a weapons depot.
"The strikes were carried out in response to Hezbollah’s attempted attack yesterday in the Ali Taher Ridge area and to remove threats posed by Hezbollah," it said.

articles.title: China’s practical push for Middle East peace and better global governance
articles.body:
China’s practical push for Middle East peace and better global governance
As the protective umbrellas of distant powers grow increasingly tattered, and as regional wars and broken global institutions feed on each other, China is emerging as a constructive force for regional security and improved global governance.
From the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) summit in Bishkek to talks between Chinese and Egyptian leaders in Cairo, Beijing has floated a series of concrete proposals that inject a measure of certainty into a turbulent world.
 
  
 
 A loud and clear voice in Bishkek
At the 26th SCO heads-of-state summit on September 1, 2026, held amid accelerating global upheaval and the rise of unilateralism and bloc confrontation, China’s president, Xi Jinping, posed an important question: what kind of multipolarity does the world need, and how should countries help shape it? He urged leaders to shoulder historical responsibility and steer events rather than drift with them.
Marking the organization’s 25th anniversary, the Bishkek Declaration reaffirmed support for Iran’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, condemned military strikes on Iranian territory as violations of the UN Charter and international law, and insisted that conflicts be settled by political and diplomatic means.
It also called for reforming global governance so that all countries can participate, decide, and benefit equally, and rejected bloc politics and confrontation as solutions to international problems. In a climate of sustained American pressure on Iran, the SCO’s stance carries unusual weight.
 
 
 A new security architecture for the Middle East
The Middle East has long been a geopolitical tinderbox. American intervention, beginning with the first Arab-Israeli war, helped plant the seeds of lasting disorder; more recent Israeli and American actions against Iran have only deepened the instability.
In talks with Egypt’s president, Abdel-Fattah al-Sisi, Mr Xi outlined a four-point proposal for a new regional security framework.
First, the region’s peoples must take charge of their own destiny and resist outside interference, an implicit rebuke to decades of American meddling.
Second, security requires comprehensive approaches, with the Palestinian question remaining central rather than being sidelined, as in the Abraham Accords that isolated Iran while bypassing the core issue.
Third, lasting peace rests on development; shared economic interests can dry up the soil in which conflict grows.
Fourth, outside powers should abandon double standards and let the United Nations play a genuine role.
Taken together, the four points sketch a security order based on common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security—distinct from arrangements designed primarily to preserve American primacy, and closer to what most regional states say they want.
 
   
  
 From idea to results: The Global Governance Initiative’s first year
A year after Mr. Xi launched the Global Governance Initiative on the 80th anniversary of the United Nations, nearly 160 countries and international organizations have endorsed it. More than 60, including Iran, have joined the “Friends of Global Governance” group.
An International Organization for Mediation, proposed by China, is now operating. A World Data Organization and a World Artificial Intelligence Co-operation Organization have been established in China, and the city of Xiamen is bidding to host the secretariat of the agreement on marine biodiversity.
These steps suggest that Beijing is trying, in practice, to move global governance away from zero-sum thinking toward arrangements that are fairer and more inclusive.
Looking east rather than west reveals a different worldview. China speaks of harmony and mutual benefit, not of winners and losers.
While some powers weave exclusive security nets and brandish the threat of maximum pressure, China uses bilateral and multilateral channels to manage differences through dialogue, to replace coercive hegemony with shared security, and to pursue stability through development.
That approach is making China an increasingly important source of steadiness in an unsettled world.

articles.title: What the US militarisation of Latin America could look like
articles.body:
What the US militarisation of Latin America could look like
More US military involvement and larger regional defence budgets mean less social spending and worse democracy outcomes.
Latin America is seeing growing military activity by the United States. Under the umbrella of the Americas Counter-Cartel Coalition (ACCC), launched by President Donald Trump in March, US forces are carrying out strikes on vessels suspected of drug trafficking, while US officials are deepening ties and cooperation with Latin American militaries.
This reflects the growing push from Washington towards militarisation of the region, as left-wing politics decline. For Latin America, this may spell the return of coercive US policies.
The projection of US military power, whether through coordinated operations, US boots on the ground or the use of regional bases, will not help improve regional security and fight crime. If anything, it could undermine democracy and usher in more violence and instability.
Return of the Monroe Doctrine
Apart from the US, the ACCC includes 17 Latin American and Caribbean nations: Argentina, Bahamas, Belize, Bolivia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Guyana, Guatemala, Paraguay, Jamaica, Panama, Trinidad and Tobago, Honduras, El Salvador, the Dominican Republic, Colombia and Peru.
Although Venezuela is not officially part of the coalition, it appears it has opened up its territory for US operations. With its informal participation, the ACCC is able to complete the “Andean arc”, which accounts for the entirety of the cocaine production distributed and sold in the US and Europe. This is also where many of the region’s organised crime groups operate.
But the coalition appears to be about more than just narcotics. Trump has said that the ACCC’s mandate is to counter “malign foreign influences from outside the Western Hemisphere” – a veiled reference to China.
The fact that the ACCC was created in Florida just two months after the US army had carried out a ground operation in Venezuela and deposed its president, Nicolas Maduro, was also significant.
Another step in that direction came on August 4 , when the US Southern Command (SOUTHCOM) announced the creation of the Western Hemisphere Joint Task Force, which will “synchronise U.S. military operations with allies and partners to counter threats, strengthen regional security and respond rapidly to crises across the Western Hemisphere”. The new task force will integrate command and control of the 18 members of the ACCC.
Washington is clearly seeking to reassert coercive hegemony over the region. It wants to exert greater influence and control over security and defence decisions in the region, in what appears to be a resurrection of the 1823 Monroe Doctrine, now renamed the Trump Corollary.
Militarisation of Latin America
Recent operations in the region have shed light on what a renewed US force projection might look like. In June, Trump revealed on Truth Social that the US army, acting in coordination with Venezuelan authorities, carried out an air strike targeting Hector Guerrero Flores, leader of the criminal gang, Tren de Aragua, in Bolivar state. In a statement, the Venezuelan government later acknowledged the joint action by both countries.
In late August and early September, the newly created Western Hemisphere Joint Task Force attacked several suspected vessels, killing at least two people. This was a continuation of the “Southern Spear” operation, which to date has killed at least 220 people with no investigation launched into whether they were all indeed involved in drug trafficking.
Added to this is the announcement made by Secretary of Defence, Pete Hegseth, that newly inaugurated Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella has authorised the US to conduct military operations in Colombia “to combat narco-terrorism”.
All of this means, the US is seeking greater military reach in Latin America, whether in the form of bilateral cooperation through joint operations or unilateral action involving overflights of the countries’ territories and even access to national military bases. There will likely be US troops on the ground involved in operations to neutralise whatever activities the US perceives as a threat.
Latin America is not new to US military intervention. During the Cold War, Washington was extensively involved in mostly covert activity in the region, but there were also overt operations, such as the invasion of the Bay of Pigs in Cuba and of the island nation of Grenada. In many cases, the civilian population faced violence as a result of the US interventions.
After the Cold War, US involvement took the shape of anti-drug campaigns, which similarly did not produce positive outcomes for local communities. Take the example of Plan Colombia (2000-2015), which was meant to combat drug trafficking and leftist insurgent groups.
Although it contributed to the weakening of insurgent organisations, it also produced a lot of violence, including by the US-trained Colombian military, which was accused of killing thousands of civilians and claiming they were rebels to “show results”. US troops stationed in Colombia as part of training programmes were also accused of raping dozens of Colombian women and girls and smuggling drugs and weapons.
Plan Colombia, which received $10bn in US funding, ended up militarising Colombia’s security agenda, intensifying armed conflicts and cartel violence, as well as the persecution of union leaders, peasants and the civilian population. It failed to stop the proliferation of coca plantations.
Given the past historical record, the US push for the militarisation of Latin American states and a greater military presence in the region is unlikely to bring more security.
Impact on Latin American societies
The effect of greater US military engagement in the region will not be limited to the security sector only.
Washington has made clear that membership in the ACCC should translate into greater national spending on defence. That means national budgets will be thrown out of balance and resources will be diverted away from vital sectors such as education, health care, housing and social security. Worsening social services provision will likely lead to more public discontent.
Then there is the question of sovereignty. The US will seek to influence the design of security and defence policies—particularly with regard to maintaining internal security and the scope of military cooperation. Washington can and will put pressure on governments and legislatures to align with its agenda.
The fact that US officials have insisted that ACCC member countries withdraw from the International Criminal Court does not bode well for transparency and accountability. Clearly, the aim is to ensure impunity for US armed forces and their allies.
It is highly likely that a lack of transparency and accountability will exacerbate the authoritarian trend that has been emerging in Latin American politics, with well-known consequences: weakening of institutions, increased discretionary power, the erosion of the rule of law, and, consequently, a decline in citizens’ quality of life.
For the Trump administration, the ACCC may be an important foreign policy win. But for Latin American societies, it is yet another threat to their fragile democratic institutions.
The views expressed in this article are the author’s own and do not necessarily reflect Al Jazeera’s editorial stance.

articles.title: British military medics test NATO wartime care in Estonia
articles.body:
British military medical personnel have taken part in a major NATO exercise in Estonia designed to test casualty care, evacuation and medical support during large-scale operations, Cyber & Specialist Operations Command has said.
Exercise Vigorous Warrior 26 ran from 8 to 20 June and brought together more than 2,000 personnel from 32 NATO Allied and partner nations. The UK deployed a 50-strong tri-Service medical force alongside other British military personnel. The British contingent included an Aeromedical Staging Unit from RAF Tactical Medical Wing and Army Reserve personnel from 144 (Parachute) Medical Squadron, part of 16 Medical Regiment.
Brigadier Chris Wright, Head of Medical Operations and Capability, said: “Exercise Vigorous Warrior is an important opportunity for UK Defence Medical personnel to train with our NATO Allies here in Estonia and demonstrate how we contribute to collective defence.
“Medical support is fundamental to operational effectiveness. By testing casualty care, patient movement and medical logistics in a realistic multinational scenario, we are strengthening our ability to support personnel on operations and improving interoperability across the Alliance.
“No one nation can meet every challenge alone. Exercises like this help ensure that, when NATO needs to act together, our medical systems, people and processes are ready to work together.”
Personnel tested Role 1 medical capability, which provides immediate frontline treatment including lifesaving care, stabilisation and basic primary care. British teams also supported patient movement and evacuation activity across the exercise.
The UK contingent trialled Mercury, the British frontline medical application designed to allow medical records to be accessed in remote locations even where an online connection is unavailable. Personnel also observed demonstrations involving uncrewed ground and aerial vehicles being used to evacuate patients, while UK Medical Communications and Information Systems specialists supported use of NATO’s new Medical Management Application patient-tracking software.
British medical personnel worked at the Patient Evacuation Coordination Centre and provided five nurses to support a German medical facility. UK personnel also led a three-day NATO Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Emergency Medical Treatment course for 24 students from 15 nations, supported by personnel from Canada, the United States and the Czech Republic.
The exercise covered the full patient pathway from point of injury through stabilisation, evacuation and onward treatment. Activity included casualty handling, medical logistics, blood resupply, civil-military cooperation and aeromedical evacuation.
The training also incorporated lessons from recent conflicts, including the need for military medical organisations to work with civilian healthcare systems during a crisis.
Exercise Vigorous Warrior is held every two years and hosted by a different NATO member. The 2026 iteration in Estonia was intended to test how allied medical systems would operate together during a large-scale operational scenario.

articles.title: More than 140 killed amid Houthi offensive in Yemen
articles.body:
Breadcrumb
More than 140 killed amid Houthi offensive in Yemen
Fighting between Yemeni government forces and Iran-backed Houthi rebels in southwest Yemen killed more than 140 combatants between midday Saturday and early Sunday morning, military sources said.
Two military officials with the Saudi-backed government forces told AFP that 84 of their troops were killed, mostly in missile attacks, while four Houthi military sources said 57 rebel fighters were killed in the same period.
Days-long clashes have erupted in Yemen over control of a gateway to the Red Sea in the deadliest fighting in the Arabian Peninsula country since a 2022 ceasefire between the two sides collapsed in July.
Beginning on Thursday, the Houthis launched an offensive aiming to cut off the government-held port city of Mokha, under fire for weeks, and advance towards areas bordering the Bab al-Mandab chokepoint at the southern entrance to the Red Sea.
According to an AFP tally compiled using various military and medical sources from both sides of the conflict, more than 300 combatants and some civilians have been killed since the start of the Houthi assault on Thursday.
One military official with the internationally recognised government based in Aden said fighting had subsided in the early hours of Sunday morning.
The military official said government "forces were able to establish positions for themselves north of Hays after advancing in the area", referring to a frontline district less than 30 kilometres inland from the Red Sea coast.
But the official added the Houthis had advanced west of Taiz, south of Hays, in their push towards the Bab al-Mandab.
With Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz to commercial ships, the Bab al-Mandab chokepoint has gained importance as a transit route for oil from Saudi Arabia, the world's biggest exporter of crude.
In July, a fragile truce between the Houthis and Yemen's government fell apart after the rebels welcomed an Iranian plane to the capital Sanaa, setting off a spate of attacks.
The fighting between the Iran-backed Houthis and government troops supported by US ally Saudi Arabia signals the emergence of a new front in the wider Middle East war, which broke out in late February with US-Israeli strikes on Iran.
The Houthis have also announced a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia and have begun targeting its ships and territory.

articles.title: Israeli strikes kill four in Lebanon after alleged Hezbollah drone launch
articles.body:
Israeli strikes kill four in Lebanon after alleged Hezbollah drone launch
Israeli air strikes on southern Lebanon Sunday killed four people, two of them women, the country's health ministry said. Israel's military said that the strikes were a response to an alleged Hezbollah drone launch targeting troops in the Israeli-occupied "security zone" in the country's south.
Lebanon said Israeli air strikes in southern Lebanon killed four people on Sunday in the latest escalation despite a months-long ceasefire.
Israel alleged that the strikes were in response to Hezbollah launching drones against its troops in the country's Israeli-occupied south.
Lebanon's health ministry reported two people killed in south Lebanon's Nabatieh al-Fawqa and two women killed in nearby Arab Salim.
It said 20 other people, including several women and three children, were wounded in those locations as well as in the city of Nabatieh and the town of Kfar Rumman, adding that the toll was provisional.
Watch moreUNIFIL peacekeepers patrol south Lebanon, caught between Israel and Hezbollah
Israel's army said it was striking south Lebanon after Hezbollah fighters launched two drones towards Israeli soldiers operating in Israel's self-declared "security zone" in the south. It did not report any troop casualties.
Shortly before the statement, Israel's military had issued its first "evacuation" notice in Lebanon in several weeks, warning residents near a building it identified as a Hezbollah "facility" in Arab Salim to leave their homes of an attack on the site.
It did not issue warnings for other areas where strikes were reported.
Lebanon's state-run National News Agency (NNA) said that after the Israeli warning for the building, "enemy warplanes launched a strike on another house, destroying it" and killing the two women.
It said the Israeli military subsequently "carried out a strike on the home" threatened in the evacuation warning.
'Security zone'
The NNA said a strike in Nabatieh al-Fawqa destroyed part of the Ghandour hospital, adding that it had been out of service for years.
It also said a heavy air strike on Nabatieh city targeted a historical building and damaged offices belonging to state finance and agriculture authorities, while shops and cafes in the vicinity were also damaged.
It also reported a strike on a motorcycle in the area.
Lebanon was drawn into the Middle East war in March after Hezbollah attacked Israel in response to the US-Israeli war against the Shiite group's ally Iran.
Israel responded with airstrikes and a ground invasion that Lebanon says have killed more than 4,300 people and driven more than a million more from their homes.
Israeli troops are still operating inside a self-declared "security zone" around 10 kilometres deep inside Lebanon along the border. Israel in June released an updated map expanding this occupied zone.
Violence has lessened since a US-Iran memorandum of understanding on the broader conflict in June, while Israel and Lebanon signed a framework agreement later that month.
But Lebanon still reports Israeli strikes, artillery shelling and broad demolitions of civilian buildings in southern villages and towns.
On Friday, Israeli strikes in the country's south and east killed four people, including an 18-year-old woman, authorities said, as Israel said it struck Hezbollah targets in response to a drone launch towards its soldiers.
Earlier this week, Israel said it had taken "operational control" of the strategic Ali al-Taher ridge near Nabatieh.
Hezbollah has not commented on the announcement or confirmed that Israel has captured the site.
Also this week, the International Committee of the Red Cross facilitated the transfer to Lebanon of five people detained by Israel.
Israel and Lebanon began direct negotiations after the latest hostilities erupted, with fresh talks expected this month, though no date has been announced.
(FRANCE 24 with AFP)

articles.title: Poland scrambles aircraft over suspected airspace breach
articles.body:
Polish Operational Command has dispatched a military helicopter to verify a suspected violation of Polish airspace by an unidentified object approaching from the direction of Belarus, the command stated on Friday.
Announcing the activity, the Operational Command of the Armed Forces Branches said the work is being conducted through the Air Operations Centre and Air Component Command, and involves checking radar system records covering the area.
It said: “Due to suspicion of a violation of the airspace of the Republic of Poland by an unidentified object approaching from the direction of Belarus, the Operational Command of the Armed Forces Branches, through the Air Operations Centre and Air Component Command, is conducting verification activities. As part of the verification of radar system records in the area, a military helicopter has been dispatched.”
The command was careful to set out what it does not yet know. It said: “The ongoing actions aim to confirm the nature of the registered object and rule out, among other possibilities, that the registered signal was the result of meteorological phenomena or anomalies.”
It added that no activity by Russian long-range aviation connected to strikes on targets in Ukraine had been observed in recent hours, that the situation is being continuously monitored, and that further information will follow once verification is complete and the details of the incident confirmed.
The reference to weather is not a throwaway line, though, as Radar returns can be generated by temperature inversions, precipitation, flocks of birds and a range of atmospheric conditions, and a command that scrambles aircraft every time a return appears will exhaust its crews and its credibility in short order.
A great many of the airspace incidents Poland has dealt with over the past three years have occurred during Russian strike packages against western Ukraine, when Polish and allied aircraft are launched as a precaution and objects periodically stray across the border. The absence of that activity means whatever was registered is unlikely to be a strayed cruise missile or a drone drifting off course from an ongoing attack.
Poland has repeatedly scrambled aircraft in response to Russian strikes on Ukraine, and objects have crossed into Polish territory on several occasions, including a missile that killed two people at Przewodów in November 2022, which was subsequently assessed as a Ukrainian air defence round.
The direction of approach carries its own significance of couyrse as Belarus hosts Russian forces and has been the origin of a range of hybrid activity directed at Poland, including the sustained pressure on the border through organised migration since 2021, and Polish forces maintain a substantial presence along that frontier.

articles.title: Zelensky Opens Third Round of Kyiv Talks With UK, France, Germany
articles.body:
President Volodymyr Zelensky announced on Sunday, Sept. 6, that following two bilateral discussion rounds with US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, talks expanded into a third session joined by representatives from the UK, France, and Germany.
Speaking to reporters after concluding discussions with the US delegation, Zelensky thanked US President Donald Trump’s special envoys for traveling to Ukraine, noting that the trip fulfilled their earlier commitment and represented their first official visit to the Ukrainian capital.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
“I thank Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff for being in Ukraine. They promised us [to visit Ukraine], and this is their first visit to our capital,” Zelensky said, according to Ukrinform.
Zelensky expressed gratitude to the US and Trump for facilitating the American delegation’s trip to Kyiv following their prior meetings in Russia. He confirmed that the two sides had completed two panel discussions, with a formal press briefing scheduled for later in the day.
“I am very glad that we are now moving to the third discussion. It will be with representatives of the leaders of Great Britain, France, and Germany,” Zelensky said, highlighting the unified stance among Western partners.
“We are very grateful that the Europeans are with us today and that we are in the circle of such nations. For us, it is very important to do everything so that this war ends. Here, we are all on the same side.”
Ukraine, US Plan Winter Aid and Post-War Guarantees in Kyiv
The president stressed that all participants share the common objective of ending the conflict through a durable and just settlement that permanently prevents any possibility of renewed Russian aggression against Ukraine.
“We all very much want there to be no war, no suffering, no loss of life, and for this war to end in a just peace for all of us, ending in such a way that there will never be any opportunity for the renewal of Russia’s aggression against Ukraine,” Zelensky said.
“And we must do everything to ensure this. I believe every such meeting, every fundamental meeting, will bring peace closer.”
Negotiations and envoys’ arrival
The multilateral consultations follow the official opening of negotiations earlier, when Zelensky met Witkoff and Kushner in Kyiv.
Upon their arrival at Kyiv’s central railway station, the US envoys were welcomed by senior Ukrainian officials, including Head of the Office of the President Kyrylo Budanov, First Deputy Head Sergiy Kyslytsya, Head of the Foreign Intelligence Service (SZRU) Rustem Umerov, and parliamentary faction leader Davyd Arakhamia.
The Kyiv diplomatic marathon follows a three-hour-and-10-minute meeting between Russian President Vladimir Putin and the US envoys at the Kremlin on Saturday evening, Sept. 5. During the Moscow talks, Russian officials discussed settlement proposals and bilateral commercial projects, with Putin agreeing to halt strikes on Kyiv for three days while rejecting a broader frontline ceasefire.

articles.title: How are NATO DIANA innovators improving wound care on the front lines?
articles.body:
Combat wound care and management have come a long way over the last few decades. And while advances in trauma care have helped save countless lives on the battlefield, preventing infection and supporting recovery after the initial injury can be just as important.
In operational environments where evacuation may not be possible and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is an increasing concern, there is a growing need for technologies that improve the way we treat wounds in the battlefield.
Innovators in NATO DIANA’s 2026 cohort are helping to meet that need by developing new approaches to wound care. From light-activated antimicrobial therapies to phage-based precision therapeutics and treatments, innovative solutions could revolutionise wound care for both civilian trauma patients and military personnel.
GutSee – Decoding the microbiome to treat infections
GutSee Health is a UK biotechnology company pioneering precision therapies for bacterial diseases. Its proprietary AI platform uses microbiome data to create precision treatments based on bacteriophage therapy. Phages are naturally occurring viruses that seek out and destroy specific bacteria without harming beneficial ones. This makes them useful for treating a variety of problems, from infected battlefield injuries to ongoing gut conditions like irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD).
Although the science behind phage therapy is well established, developing these treatments remains fragmented, manual and focused on individual patients.
GutSee’s platform brings four key stages into one integrated process. First, it matches bacterial strains with the phages most likely to destroy them. Second, it predicts how bacteria may evolve and mutate, helping treatments stay ahead of emerging resistance. Third, it designs mixtures of several phages combined with beneficial bacteria to improve the overall bacterial balance rather than simply remove a harmful pathogen. Finally, it connects treatment design with manufacturing and clinical use. Together, these stages form a continuous learning cycle that improves treatment recommendations, accelerating therapy development by up to 98% compared with traditional laboratory-heavy processes.
GutSee is initially focusing on combat and civilian wound infections, working with NATO, governments and foundations, with support from the Ukrainian government. Longer term, GutSee plans to license its platform for further areas, including gut disorders and oncology.
LightOx – Using light to help control wound infections
LightOx is developing light-activated treatments that help kill harmful bacteria that colonise wounds. They produce a simple gel that can be applied directly to a wound. The gel is activated by a light, and the treatment helps kill harmful bacteria in a targeted way, right where the infection is developing.
In battlefield injuries, bacteria can quickly enter damaged tissue and cause infections that slow healing and increase the risk of complications, including sepsis, amputation, or even death. This is especially challenging when common antibiotics stop working against drug-resistant bacteria. LightOx’s approach offers a tool to help control infection in wounds while injured personnel await further treatment, while also fighting AMR.
Earlier this year, LightOx was recognised for its light-activated treatment for infected wounds, with an Outstanding Achievement Award at the Medilink Healthcare Business Awards 2026.
Deep Breathe – Helping medics detect hidden chest injuries faster
In battlefield trauma, injuries to the lungs or chest can be difficult to spot without hospital equipment, but failing to detect them can delay critical care. Deep Breathe, based in Canada, have developed a solution involving a portable ultrasound that frontline medical teams can use to detect serious chest and torso injuries faster, as well internal abdominal bleeding.
Deep Breathe combine ultrasound with AI that recognise signs of injuries such as a collapsed lung, bleeding in the chest, or bruising of lung tissue. Designed to work on phones or tablets and in places with limited or no connectivity, the technology could help medics make faster, more informed decisions closer to the point of injury, improving triage in remote areas and difficult environments.
By bringing this kind of support closer to the battlefield – at the point-of-injury – Deep Breathe’s solution could help improve diagnosis and treatment, avoiding unnecessary invasive procedures, and speeding up life-saving decisions when every second matters.
Biocellis – Instant detection of biological and chemical agents
After a Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) attack, effective treatment requires a quick response and knowledge of the intoxicating agent. Biocellis is a company from France that has developed an ultra-sensitive diagnostic testing system that can rapidly detect and identify biological and chemical agents.
Traditionally, rapid testing methods sacrifice sensitivity and most sensitive tests do not provide results fast enough. Biocellis has patented a bioluminescence immunoassays platform that delivers laboratory grade sensitivity in less than 60 seconds. The technology uses a compact, portable format that is ideal for point-of-care and high-throughput screening.
Rapid and reliable detection helps clinicians treat patients with the most effective remedies available. Biocellis helps medical professionals understand what they are up against so that they can quickly provide the treatment and care that patients need.
These technologies are already filling some of the most urgent gaps in battlefield medicine. By giving frontline medical teams better tools to save lives and improve care when conditions are at their most challenging.
Through NATO DIANA, these innovators gain access to the tools and resources they need to take their promising, cutting-edge technologies from concept to real-world use. Through expertise from technical and defence mentors, opportunities to test their technologies, and access to operational exercises like Vigorous Warrior, innovators are supported by DIANA to ensure their solutions are not only technically strong, but deployable and relevant in the demanding environments where they are needed most.
Source: diana.nato.int

articles.title: Russian Strike Hits Dnipro Logistics Warehouses, Injuring 2
articles.body:
Russian forces launched an attack on the city of Dnipro on Sunday, Sept. 6, striking warehouses operated by a logistics company and injuring at least two people, Dnipropetrovsk Regional Military Administration Head Oleksandr Hanzha reported.
The strike ignited a large fire at the commercial storage facilities, according to Hanzha’s statement on Telegram.

Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
“The enemy attacked Dnipro. As a result of the strike, a fire broke out at the warehouses of a logistics company,” Hanzha initially stated.
In a subsequent update, Hanzha confirmed that two civilians sustained injuries in the attack and were receiving necessary medical treatment, while emergency services worked to contain and extinguish the blaze.
Evening drone strikes kill five across four regions
The daytime attack on Dnipro follows a wave of Russian drone strikes late Saturday, Sept. 5, that killed at least five civilians and injured 17 others across the Kharkiv, Kyiv, Zaporizhzhia, and Khmelnytskyi regions.
In the Kharkiv region, a Russian jet-powered drone hit a private residential area in central Chuhuiv, killing three members of a single family: a 45-year-old man, a 19-year-old woman, and an 11-year-old boy. The strike destroyed a private home, an outbuilding, and a garage, while severely injuring a woman and leaving three other residents suffering from acute stress reactions.
In the Kyiv region, Russian drones targeted the village of Lisne in the Bucha district, setting two private houses on fire. The attack killed two people, injured one, and damaged five homes alongside three vehicles.
US Sanctions Chief Joins Moscow Talks as Putin Cites War Goals
In Zaporizhzhia, multiple drone strikes damaged residential houses and an administrative building late Saturday, injuring at least six people, including an elderly woman, while sparking several structure fires.
In Khmelnytskyi, a Russian drone struck a multi-story apartment block, injuring seven residents and destroying stairwells and structural floor slabs. Concurrent drone strikes also damaged commercial enterprises in the Khmelnytskyi district, triggering fires that were later brought under control by rescue crews.

articles.title: Kremlin sees ‘atmosphere of trust’ in Putin’s talks with Witkoff and Kushner
articles.body:
Kremlin sees ‘atmosphere of trust’ in Putin’s talks with Witkoff and Kushner
The talks that Russian President Vladimir Putin had with US President Donald Trump’s envoys on Saturday are indicative of an “atmosphere of trust” between Moscow and Washington, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov has said.
Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have arrived in Kiev, where they are meeting with the Ukrainian leadership as part of US efforts to mediate a peace deal between Russia and Ukraine.
Speaking to Russian journalist Pavel Zarubin on Sunday, Peskov stated that “there is indeed an atmosphere of trust, at least with respect to this communication channel, [and] it is growing stronger.”
The official added that the “exchange of such greetings [between the Russian president and foreign dignitaries] is extended… when there are messages that the head of state deems necessary to convey.”
Commenting on Saturday’s negotiations between Putin and Witkoff and Kushner, which lasted over three hours and included formal discussions as well as an informal exchange over lunch, Kremlin aide Yury Ushakov told reporters that the “conversation was substantive, constructive, extremely candid and trusting.”
According to the Russian official, the US negotiators presented a “number of considerations regarding possible paths toward a settlement” of the Ukraine conflict.
Ushakov revealed that the Russian president and Trump’s envoys had also discussed economic cooperation and potential “major, mutually beneficial Russian-American projects.” He characterized the talks as “timely and very useful for both sides,” with Putin and Trump intending to continue personal contacts as well as the diplomatic work being conducted by Witkoff and Kushner.
The Russian president earlier praised his US counterpart for his sustained efforts to end the hostilities between Moscow and Kiev.
Ahead of the US negotiators’ departure for Kiev, Putin ordered a three-day hiatus in strikes on the Ukrainian capital to allow Witkoff and Kushner to safely carry out their mission.

articles.title: Report: Russian historian detained at Ben Gurion Airport over alleged Iran espionage links
articles.body:
Russian-Israeli historian Artyom Kirpichonok was detained at Ben Gurion Airport on suspicion of espionage linked to Iran, according to reports in Russian media.
The opposition news outlet Meduza reported over the weekend that Kirpichonok, who holds both Israeli and Russian citizenship but lives in Russia, was arrested after arriving in Israel. According to the report, investigators suspect him of contact with a foreign intelligence operative and involvement in influence activity directed against Israel.
His lawyer, Inna Labedinskaya-Katz, told the Russian newspaper Izvestia that the case involves several espionage-related charges whose details are classified. “This is the most serious type of offense concerning harm to state security,” she said.
Family members told Meduza that the allegations were false and stemmed from Kirpichonok’s ties to Russia. At the same time, relatives said they understood that investigators suspected him of contact with an agent connected to Iran or Lebanon.
Kirpichonok, 51, was born in St. Petersburg and immigrated to Israel in the 1990s. He studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and later returned to Russia, where he has lived since 2005.
Over the years, he has become a vocal critic of Israel and Zionism. His books include A People’s History of Israel, which deals with the history of Palestine and the establishment of the Jewish state, and Israel: The Road to Catastrophe, which examines Israeli domestic and foreign policy through a historical lens
The Iran connection also appears in Kirpichonok’s travel history. Izvestia reported that he visited Iran several times despite being an Israeli citizen. In 2018, he reportedly spent about two weeks there and documented the trip extensively on social media.
His relatives argued that those visits had not previously triggered action by Israeli authorities. They said Kirpichonok returned to Israel several times after traveling to Iran without being questioned about the matter.
Labedinskaya-Katz said Kirpichonok was arrested by the Shin Bet and is being held in a secure wing. She also alleged that he complained of harsh treatment during interrogation, including sleep deprivation, constant lighting in his cell, being forced into uncomfortable positions and questioning under pressure and threats.
Those allegations have not been independently verified.
Supporters in Russia have since formed a campaign demanding his release and are collecting signatures for petitions to be sent to Israeli consulates in Moscow and St. Petersburg.
The group claims Kirpichonok had been invited to Israel to lecture at a conference and now suspects the invitation may have been a trap.
Former Russian lawmaker Darya Mitina has also expressed concern that Kirpichonok could become a bargaining chip in relations between Israel and Russia.

articles.title: Trump's first call after peace talks briefing will be Putin, source says
articles.body:
U.S. President Donald Trump is expected to speak with Russian President Vladimir Putin after being briefed by his representatives on the latest round of peace talks in Kyiv and Moscow, a U.S. official told the Kyiv Independent.
Trump will consult with his envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, before calling Putin and then speaking with President Volodymyr Zelensky, the official said. The calls will likely take place on Sept. 7.
Witkoff and Kushner made their first visit to Kyiv on Sept. 6, where they met with Zelensky and held talks with his team a day after sitting down to talks with Putin in Moscow. The efforts are intended to advance negotiations on ending Russia's war against Ukraine.
The White House said the Moscow talks included "substantive plans for next steps," though neither side announced a breakthrough. In a press conference following the talks, Zelensky indicated that the recent peace push would not lead to an end to the war anytime soon, while Kushner indicated to reporters that the U.S. hoped to return to trilateral negotiations with both Russia and Ukraine.
The Kyiv meeting marked Witkoff and Kushner's first visit to Ukraine. The pair's arrival came after repeated invitations from Kyiv, with the envoys having previously traveled repeatedly to Moscow for meetings with Putin and other senior Russian officials.
Their talks with Zelensky followed months of stalled diplomacy amid the U.S. war against Iran. Previous U.S.-led negotiations centered on territory, security guarantees, and the terms of any ceasefire or peace agreement, with little progress achieved.
Trump has previously spoken directly with Putin following meetings between the Russian leader and U.S. envoys. Trump has also held calls with Putin before and after meeting with Ukrainian representatives, including his in-person meeting with Zelensky in Mar-a-Lago in December 2025.

articles.title: Witkoff, Kushner arrive in Ukraine after Putin talks in push for peace
articles.body:
Trump envoys say Ukraine peace talks were "very meaningful" after Moscow visit
President Trump's White House special envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner held "encouraging" talks in Kyiv, part of a trip that began in Moscow in the latest push to end more than 4½ years of Russia's full-scale invasion.
The trip marks the first time the envoys have traveled to Ukraine since Mr. Trump returned to office with a pledge to solve the conflict.
After two rounds of discussion with the U.S. officials, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the goal was a "just, fair peace" that would ensure there was "never an opportunity to resume aggression against Ukraine." He said the next round of talks later Sunday would bring in national security advisers from Britain, France and Germany.
"We've had very meaningful discussion, substantive, important, and we're very encouraged," Witkoff said.
Kushner said Mr. Trump sees it as important "not just to figure out how do we end the current war," but how to create the conditions for durable peace.
A senior Ukrainian official, who spoke on condition of anonymity as he was not authorized to speak publicly, told The Associated Press that much of the discussion was focused on "how to get through the winter and what can be done before then."
Witkoff and Kushner held a three-hour meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Saturday in Moscow, where they "discussed substantive plans for next steps, which will be announced in the coming weeks," according to a White House official.
Prior to Witkoff and Kushner's departure, Mr. Trump told reporters the envoys were traveling to Ukraine and Russia with a proposal to end the conflict. Mr. Trump said they had had "an idea for peace," and that "there may be a good chance that we'll do it."
After the meeting, Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said in a statement that "our American colleagues made serious preparations for this trip," and they had "also formulated a number of ideas regarding possible paths to a settlement," but did not elaborate on what those might be.
At the start of the meeting in Moscow, which was captured on video, Putin asked Kushner and Witkoff to pass on his warm wishes and gratitude to Mr. Trump, and described the situation in Ukraine as "not simple."
Ushakov added that the talks also discussed in "some detail" potential deals between the U.S. and Russia that would be "mutually beneficial."
Both Ukraine and Russia agreed Saturday to pause strikes while the envoys were in the country to allow for talks to take place.
"Putin has ordered that no strikes be carried out against Kyiv for three days," presidential spokesperson Dmitry Peskov told Russia's Tass news agency, saying the decision was tied to Witkoff and Kushner's planned visit to the Ukrainian capital. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy mirrored the decision by halting strikes until Monday.
In his Sunday prayer, Pope Leo XIV renewed his appeal for peace in Ukraine and said he hopes the negotiations will bring results.
"I hope that the efforts undertaken in recent days to resume negotiations will bear concrete fruit and make way for diplomacy," he told the gathered faithful in St. Peter's Square at the Vatican.
The White House official also told CBS News that the U.S. delegation thanked Putin for the release of U.S. Marine veteran Robert Gilman, a 32-year-old teacher who had been imprisoned in Russia since 2022. Gilman was freed and allowed to return home last month. Before his release, Gilman was hospitalized in serious condition after he had allegedly been subjected to severe mistreatment, according to Global Reach, an organization that worked to free him.
